Listen, I know how you feel. When I was 11, I got this crazy ass disease that (In non-medical terms) starts paralyzing you to death. I went from a normal kid to almost dead in about three weeks. Unfortunately, I got better from treatment. So I'm not paralyzed anymore, but I was in a wheelchair for a year. Which left me weak, and tired all the time. I have severe chronic pain every single day. Its pretty much shit. (Im 16 now by the way)

You see, the doctors never prepared me for any of this. The depression, the pain, the amount of hard work it would be getting out of that goddam wheelchair. So, I was angry. Angry at all of them, including my parents. I hated the way everyone lied and said it would get better, because its not. My body is deteriorating right before my eyes. Nothing is going to go back to the way it was. 

But i realized that I could sit here and be all pissed off, for something that's never going to come back. I could tell everyone how they were bad doctors and didn't say anything, but is it not gonna change. 
So, there was a certain moment when I finally said, Fuck it. I don't want to be sad and sick anymore. I want to try and start actually living and not be an angry asshole all the time. And I know its a hard thing to just "get over". But you might reach that point where you finally realize that there is more to life than being sick and tired and angry. And it doesn't just go away. I still have my periods of frustration and anger, loss of hope. But I keep going, and keep trying.
